Theme 079 · Characters & mascots

Shadow Puppet Theatre

Cut-paper silhouettes against a tinted, backlit screen, after the silhouette films of the 1920s. Pulse is a heron standing perfectly still in the river of a metric — the first to see the water fall — while a small human figure reaches for a glowing coral lantern.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Heron silhouette — Pulse: a still, patient watcher that moves only when it matters
  • Tinted backlight — amber = before, teal = Pulse is watching, dawn = resolved
  • Cut-paper towers — dashboards as a silhouette city with lit window-bars
  • River metric — the metric line as water; the anomaly is a waterfall
  • Cartouche — ornate black label for the anomaly readout
  • Coral lantern — the human’s action (Roll back) glowing in the dark

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Stepped cut-out poses — joints swap between 3 drawn poses at 12 fps, never tweened; pose changes land on quarter notes (0.5 s at 120 BPM)
  • Multiplane drift — 3 silhouette layers parallax at 0.3/0.6/1.0 speed, 8-bar loop, linear — the calm under the beat
  • Tint cross-fade — background gradient shifts hue over exactly 1 bar (2 s), starting on the drop and on the resolution

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: Silhouettes read at any size and feel crafted and calm — the opposite of a noisy dashboard. A heron is a natural metaphor for patient watching: motionless for ages, then one precise strike. Risk: Silhouette-only frames hide UI detail and can feel slow or melancholy; keep the data in the cartouche large and crisp, and keep the tempo up with stepped poses.

Adapt to your product: Cut your product’s key screens into silhouettes (towers, rivers, paths), pick a watchful animal for your agent, and colour the backlight with your palette to mark each story beat.

References: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lotte_Reiniger (the pioneer of silhouette animation; gesture instead of faces) · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Adventures_of_Prince_Achmed (1926 feature: cut-outs under a camera, multiplane, colour tinting)
